desc:
In one move you may choose any element of nums and decrease it by 1. Elements may become negative.

The array is a valley zigzag if one of the two holds (indices start at 0):

  • every element at an even index is strictly smaller than each of its adjacent elements, or
  • every element at an odd index is strictly smaller than each of its adjacent elements.

Return the minimum number of moves needed to turn nums into a valley zigzag.

nums = [1,2,3]      -> 2
nums = [9,6,1,6,2]  -> 4
hints: There are only two shapes to aim for: even indices are the valleys, or odd indices are the valleys. Solve each shape separately and take the cheaper.
Lowering an element that is meant to be a peak can never help anybody. Only valleys need to be lowered.

For a valley at index i, look at both neighbours. It must end up at most min(left, right) - 1, so its cost is max(0, nums[i] - min(left, right) + 1); a missing neighbour is ignored. Neighbours are peaks and stay unchanged.
editorial: Fix which parity holds the valleys. Peaks are never changed (decreasing a peak only makes its neighbours' job harder), so every valley is independent: it must be strictly less than the original values of its one or two neighbours, which costs max(0, nums[i] - min(neighbours) + 1) moves. Sum this over all valleys of that parity.
Repeat for the other parity and return the smaller total. The greedy part is that each valley goes exactly one below its smaller neighbour, no further. Time O(n), space O(1).
solution:
def movesToZigzag(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    INF = 10 ** 9
    best = None
    for start in (0, 1):
        cost = 0
        for i in range(start, n, 2):
            left = nums[i - 1] if i > 0 else INF
            right = nums[i + 1] if i + 1 < n else INF
            m = min(left, right)
            if nums[i] >= m:
                cost += nums[i] - m + 1
        best = cost if best is None else min(best, cost)
    return best
